dataFiles: src/geometry/curves.ts NERVE_COURSES (the 12 course geometry records added by run run-mtzc5coc-ug6z: waypoints, tubeRadius, calibreMm, foramen, anchorId)
src/data/structures/pons.json + medulla.json + midbrain.json + diencephalon.json (the nuc-* and surf-cn*-exit records the 12 nerves link)
src/data/syndromes/*.json (26 cards; the 26 supply ids and the vascularTerritory text)
src/data/taxonomy.json (14 vessel + 12 nerve + cranial-nerve-nucleus laterality/name entries)
src/assets/anatomy/*.glb committed meshes (bounding boxes read, not re-baked)
scope.notAuditedHere: the 15 plate manifests + SVGs are owned by the plate auditor; only the three plate facts that sit inside this area (the CN III rootlet label, the CN IV rootlet label, the absence of any vessel label) were checked and they are reported as ok below.
scope.geometryMethod: canonical space x = +patient-left, y = +superior (anchor-warped to levels.json), z = +anterior, 1 au = 1.2 mm (docs/VASC_INVENTORY.md §2, docs/REALISM_PLAN.md §3 AMENDMENT A). origin3d / size3d / waypoints / levels are authored in RECORD space; the committed meshes are baked in the same space EXCEPT that the y axis was piecewise-linearly warped onto the level anchors at registration (scripts/lib/register.mjs §3.2, warp knots 1220.63→-50, 1251.04→-24, 1274.79→+4, 1287.71→+20, 1300.57→+38 in assets-src/bp3d/canonical/registration-summary.json). CONSEQUENCE USED THROUGHOUT: x and z are uniform at 1 au = 1.2 mm and are therefore directly comparable between a record and its committed mesh; y is NOT, so no finding in this file claims a y error from a mesh bbox alone. Levels[] and origin3d.y are compared against levels.json anchors instead.

findings.claimed: supply includes "syn-lateral-medullary" (Lateral medullary syndrome)
findings.expected: no lateral-medullary entry; the MCA cannot supply the dorsolateral medulla, which is PICA/vertebral territory
findings.basis: syn-lateral-medullary.vascularTerritory = "Posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), usually occluded at its vertebral origin; occasionally the vertebral artery directly"; the syndrome's own structures[] are all medullary (nuc-spinal-trigeminal, nuc-ambiguus, nuc-dmv, nuc-solitarius-caudal, tract-icp, tract-spinothalamic, nuc-medullary-reticular). The MCA record's own contextNote admits the entry exists only because the card "cites the MCA among its alternatives", but the card text contains no MCA mention at all. The MCA record's own territory[] contains no medullary structure.
findings.suggestedFix: delete "syn-lateral-medullary" from vasc-middle-cerebral-artery.supply (leaving the MCA's genuine syndrome associations to its clinical[] array and to the territory structures' own bloodSupply text).
findings.notes: This is the exact class of defect the dispatch named as critical: a syndrome card attached to an artery that does not supply the damaged structure. The forward index (arteriesForSyndrome) is what makes it visible in the UI, so the wrong artery is highlighted when the Wallenberg card is opened.

findings.claimed: supply includes "syn-parkinson" (Parkinson's disease)
findings.expected: no Parkinson's entry on any vessel record; the card itself declares a non-vascular cause
findings.basis: syn-parkinson.vascularTerritory = "None (degenerative alpha-synucleinopathy, not vascular)"; its structures are nuc-snc / nuc-snr, whose own bloodSupply in midbrain.json names the PCA/paramedian midbrain perforators, never the MCA. No other vessel declares syn-parkinson, so the atlas currently teaches that the MCA causes Parkinson's disease.
findings.suggestedFix: delete "syn-parkinson" from vasc-middle-cerebral-artery.supply.
findings.notes: Same defect class as VN-001; the MCA contextNote claim that the two supply entries are 'the syndrome cards whose arterial territory is named as MCA in the existing data' is false for both entries.

findings.expected: z ≈ 13–15 (inside the committed trunk's z extent [11.3, 16.8]); x = 0 already correct
findings.basis: The committed mesh vasc-basilar-artery.glb (the GLB registered for exactly this record) has bbox z [11.3, 16.8]; the record's z = 6 is 5.3 au (= 6.4 mm) POSTERIOR to the trunk's most posterior point, i.e. the anchor sits inside the pons substance rather than in the prepontine cistern where the record's own function text puts it. x and z are uniform-scaled axes, so this comparison is exact.
findings.suggestedFix: origin3d = [0, -12, 14] (mid-trunk, inside the committed mesh and inside the prepontine cistern between the pons ventral surface z ≈ 16.7 and the trunk z ∈ [11.3, 16.8]).
findings.notes: Same axis, same sign for vasc-anterior-inferior-cerebellar-artery (z = -4 vs mesh z [-5.9, 14.2]) and vasc-posterior-communicating-artery (z = 8 vs mesh z [11.6, 22.3]) - a systematic posterior bias in the z field of the circle-of-Willis/trunk records, not a one-off.

findings.expected: x ≈ 8.4 (mesh x mid-point), z ≈ 16.9 (mesh z mid-point) — at minimum inside the committed mesh on all three axes
findings.basis: The record's own mesh vasc-posterior-communicating-artery-l.glb spans x [6.0, 10.8], y [5.4, 8.2], z [11.6, 22.3] (union of the -l and -r halves: x ±[4.0, 10.8]). The record's x = 14 is 3.2 au lateral to the mesh and its z = 8 is 3.6 au posterior to it — outside the mesh on BOTH uniform-scaled axes. Every other paired artery's origin3d.x sits inside its mesh x range, so this is not a convention.
findings.suggestedFix: origin3d ≈ [8, 7, 17] (the mesh's own centre; the record's y = 22.5 can be left alone because y is warped and the level-matching anchor is what y is for).
findings.notes: The record's y = 22.5 places it centrally inside its own levels[] span (lvl-midbrain-sc +14 … lvl-thalamus-mid +28), so only x and z are reported.

findings.claimed: origin3d.z = -4
findings.expected: z ≈ +3 to +5 (the proximal basilar segment it arises from), i.e. inside the committed mesh
findings.basis: vasc-anterior-inferior-cerebellar-artery-l.glb spans z [-5.9, 14.2]; the AICA arises from the basilar at z ≈ +14 and loops through the cerebellopontine angle — the record's z = -4 places its anchor at the most posterior point of the whole element, in the petrous/cerebellar corner rather than at the basilar origin its own afferent text names. z is uniform-scaled, so the comparison is exact, and the offset (18 au = 22 mm) is the largest z error in the vessel set.
findings.suggestedFix: origin3d.z ≈ +4 (the record's y = -16 and x = 10 already sit correctly inside the mesh).
findings.notes: The AICA's afferent/efferent text and its territory[] are correct; only the anchor is adrift, so this is a rendering/localisation defect rather than a claim defect.

findings.claimed: levels = [lvl-midbrain-ic (+8), lvl-midbrain-sc (+14), lvl-post-comm (+19)]
findings.expected: the SCA's own level set must contain at least lvl-pons-rostral (+2) and lvl-pons-middle (-8), because the structures the same record declares it supplies live there
findings.basis: Internal contradiction inside one record: territory[] names ctx-cerebellum (levels lvl-olivary … lvl-pons-rostral), nuc-dentate / nuc-interposed / nuc-fastigial (levels lvl-pontomedullary, lvl-pons-caudal, lvl-pons-middle) and surf-vermis (levels lvl-olivary … lvl-pons-rostral), yet not one of those level ids appears in the artery's own levels[]. Five of the record's twelve territory entries therefore have no level on which the artery is visible — the SCA disappears exactly where its lesion is taught (the artery's origin3d.y = +8 is itself 5 levels above the dentate it supplies). The record's own clinical text ("SCA territory infarct with brainstem compression", "Nothnagel syndrome") is unreachable at every level the SCA is drawn on.
findings.suggestedFix: levels = [lvl-pons-middle, lvl-pons-rostral, lvl-midbrain-ic, lvl-midbrain-sc] (the SCA arises at lvl-pons-rostral/+2, encircles the midbrain at lvl-midbrain-ic/+8, and its medial/vermian branches reach the dentate at lvl-pons-caudal).
findings.notes: The check generalises: a script over all 14 vessels (artery.levels ∩ territory-record.levels = ∅) returns exactly three offenders — this one, VN-007 and VN-008. The same test on the MCA, ACA, PCA, PICA, AICA, vertebral, ICA, PComA, AChA, LSA and AComA returns no offender.

findings.claimed: levels = [lvl-midbrain-sc (+14), lvl-post-comm (+19), lvl-thalamus-mid (+28)]
findings.expected: at least lvl-thalamus-rostral (+36) and lvl-tel-thalamostriate (+48) added, because the record declares the body of the lateral ventricle in its territory
findings.basis: territory[] includes vent-lateral-ventricle-body, whose own levels[] in telencephalon-ventricles.json are [lvl-thalamus-rostral, lvl-tel-thalamostriate, lvl-tel-basal-ganglia]. None of the three appears in the artery's levels[], so the record simultaneously claims to supply the ventricle body and declares itself invisible at every level on which the ventricle body exists. The record's own function text ("the lateral posterior choroidal artery … supplies the choroid plexus of the body") makes the missing levels a self-contradiction, not a judgement call.
findings.suggestedFix: levels = [lvl-midbrain-sc, lvl-post-comm, lvl-thalamus-mid, lvl-thalamus-rostral, lvl-tel-thalamostriate].
findings.notes: The levels[] of vent-choroid-plexus-lateral and vent-lateral-ventricle-atrium do overlap, which is why the gap is only in the body/atrium→thalamostriate direction.

findings.claimed: levels ends at lvl-midbrain-ic (+8) while territory[] includes surf-interpeduncular-fossa
findings.expected: lvl-midbrain-sc (+14) added, or surf-interpeduncular-fossa removed from territory[]
findings.basis: surf-interpeduncular-fossa is registered at lvl-midbrain-sc (+14) only; the basilar's levels[] stop at lvl-midbrain-ic (+8). The record's own function text says the basilar "divid[es] into the two posterior cerebral arteries at the interpeduncular fossa", so the structure is a legitimate territory entry and the level set is the thing that is short by one.
findings.suggestedFix: append "lvl-midbrain-sc" to vasc-basilar-artery.levels.
findings.notes: Marked suspect rather than wrong because the interpeduncular fossa is arguably reached by the basilar apex rather than by the trunk, and the atlas may intend the trunk's levels to stop at the pontomesencephalic junction.

findings.claimed: "Terminal bifurcation into the anterior cerebral artery … and the middle cerebral artery …; medial and lateral lenticulostriate perforators (vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries) arise from the proximal segments"
findings.expected: "…; lateral lenticulostriate perforators arise from the proximal MCA (and medial lenticulostriate perforators, including the recurrent artery of Heubner, from the proximal ACA)"
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the lenticulostriate record: vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries.connections.afferent says the lateral group comes from "vasc-middle-cerebral-artery, M1 segment" and the medial group (Heubner) from "vasc-anterior-cerebral-artery, A1 segment". The ICA gives rise to neither group; the phrase "proximal segments" in the ICA record most plausibly means the proximal segments of the ACA/MCA, but as written it attributes both groups to the carotid, which is the single most common student error this atlas exists to prevent.
findings.suggestedFix: rewrite the clause as "lateral lenticulostriate perforators arise from the proximal M1 middle cerebral artery and the medial group (recurrent artery of Heubner) from the proximal A1 anterior cerebral artery".
findings.notes: The same record's territory[] correctly includes the striatum and internal capsule, which is legitimate for the ICA as the parent trunk — only the perforator attribution is wrong.

findings.claimed: supply includes "syn-hemiballismus"
findings.expected: no hemiballismus entry on the anterior choroidal artery; the subthalamic nucleus is not in its territory[] and its afferent/efferent lists never mention the subthalamic nucleus
findings.basis: The record's own field set contradicts the entry: territory[] (12 structures) contains no nuc-subthalamic, and the efferent list names the optic tract, uncus, amygdala, hippocampus, pallidum, choroidal fissure, optic radiation and posterior limb — never the subthalamic nucleus. syn-hemiballismus.vascularTerritory names the PComA first and the anterior choroidal second ("Perforating branches of the posterior communicating artery and anterior choroidal artery to the subthalamic nucleus"), so the entry traces to the card's own hedged wording rather than to this record's data; the modern account of the subthalamic supply is the posterior communicating/perforating and posterior thalamoperforating arteries, with the anterior choroidal contribution at best a variant.
findings.suggestedFix: either delete "syn-hemiballismus" from vasc-anterior-choroidal-artery.supply and leave it on vasc-posterior-communicating-artery and vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries, or add nuc-subthalamic to the AChA territory[] and state the variant explicitly in its function text. Do NOT silently keep the supply entry without one of the two.
findings.notes: Deliberately suspect, not wrong: the perforator-to-subthalamic-nucleus attribution is genuinely variable in the literature, so the defect that can be established here is the missing internal support for the claim, not the anatomy.

findings.claimed: "Tonsillomedullary and telovelotonsillar segments with medullary branches to the dorsolateral medulla …"
findings.expected: the segment list should start with the anterior medullary segment ("anterior medullary and lateral medullary segments …"), because a PICA that supplies the dorsolateral medulla and reaches the tonsil must pass through them first
findings.basis: The two named segments are the 3rd and 4th of the five standard PICA segments; the anterior medullary (p1) and lateral medullary (p2) segments — the ones that actually run beside the medulla and give the medullary perforators the record attributes to the tonsillomedullary segment — are omitted. The record's own afferent text describes the origin "at the level of the olive … before turning up", which is the anterior/lateral medullary course, so the efferent list and the afferent list describe the same vessel with different segments.
findings.suggestedFix: write "anterior medullary, lateral medullary, tonsillomedullary and telovelotonsillar segments (the five-segment scheme), with medullary branches to the dorsolateral medulla …".
findings.notes: External basis: the five-segment PICA scheme (anterior medullary, lateral medullary, tonsillomedullary, telovelotonsillar, cortical) is standard in the surgical/radiological literature — see https://radiopaedia.org/articles/posterior-inferior-cerebellar-artery and Lister et al., "Microsurgical anatomy of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery" (PubMed 7070615). Not verifiable from the repo alone, hence suspect rather than wrong.

findings.claimed: territory lists 12 structures but not surf-cn5-exit, although the record's own bloodSupply and the trigeminal record both describe SCA-nerve contact
findings.expected: surf-cn5-exit added to territory[] (and nuc-trigeminal-motor / nuc-principal-sensory-v considered), or the contact described only in prose with no territory implication
findings.basis: arteryToNerveCoverage check: for each vessel the exit landmark of every nerve that names that vessel is absent from territory[] for all four naming pairs (SCA↔nrv-cn5-trigeminal, PICA↔nrv-cn9-glossopharyngeal, MCA↔nrv-cn6-abducens, SCA↔nrv-cn4-trochlear), whereas the nucleus-level half of the same claim IS covered (AICA→surf-cn7-exit + surf-cn8-exit; PICA→surf-cn11-exit). The SCA case is the record's own claim (bloodSupply: "the artery lies immediately below the trochlear nerve and above the trigeminal root"; clinical: trigeminal neuralgia and "Nothnagel syndrome"), and the basilar record DOES make the analogous entry (surf-interpeduncular-fossa), so the convention exists in the data set.
findings.suggestedFix: add "surf-cn5-exit" (and optionally "surf-cn4-exit") to vasc-superior-cerebellar-artery.territory so the neurovascular-compression claim is machine-visible; add "surf-cn9-exit" to PICA, "surf-cn6-exit" to the basilar/MCA, "surf-cn3-exit" to the PComA/PCA.
findings.notes: Both the trigeminal record ("an elongated superior cerebellar artery loops against the nerve") and the SCA record ("aneurysms here present with a fourth-nerve palsy or with trigeminal neuralgia-like facial pain") make the claim, so the missing territory entry is a data-consistency gap rather than a false claim.

findings.claimed: synonyms = ["PCA", "arteria cerebri posterior", "P1/P2/P3 segments of the posterior cerebral artery", "calcarine artery (P3 branch)"]
findings.expected: the P-segment synonym should read "P1/P2/P3/P4 segments" (or a segment list should be added: P1 precommunicating, P2 ambient, P3 quadrigeminal, P4 cortical)
findings.basis: Terminologia Anatomica/FMA and every standard reference give the posterior cerebral artery FOUR segments, not three: P1 precommunicating, P2 postcommunicating/ambient, P3 quadrigeminal, P4 calcarine/cortical. The record's own contextNote cites the archive's own segment split ("the precommunicating P1 part … and the postcommunicating P2–P3 part"), which stops at P3, so the P4 (cortical/calcarine) segment — the one its own clinical[] describes as the calcarine branch — is named nowhere. The synonym set also lists the calcarine artery as if it were the same vessel (it is a branch, not a synonym), though the parenthetical "(P3 branch)" mitigates that. The audit brief names "PCA P1-P4" explicitly.
findings.suggestedFix: synonyms = ["PCA", "arteria cerebri posterior", "P1 precommunicating / P2 ambient / P3 quadrigeminal / P4 cortical segments", "calcarine artery (a P3/P4 branch, not a synonym)"].
findings.notes: The MCA's analogue is correct and complete ("M1/M2/M3/M4 segments"), so the omission is specific to the PCA. ACA uses "A1/A2/A3" which is the accepted three-part scheme.

findings.claimed: two identical refs entries ("Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 3rd ed., Ch. 'Cerebral Hemispheres and Vascular Supply'")
findings.expected: the duplicate removed; one entry is enough
findings.basis: The array contains the same string twice (also present on vasc-middle-cerebral-artery, whose refs repeat the same chapter back to back).
findings.suggestedFix: dedupe the refs arrays of vasc-internal-carotid-artery and vasc-middle-cerebral-artery.
findings.notes: Cosmetic, but refs are shown to the reader and the allReferences index de-duplicates, so the duplication only wastes the reader's attention.

findings.claimed: name = "Posterior medial choroidal artery" and synonyms include "posterior choroidal arteries (with its lateral companion)" and "lateral posterior choroidal artery"
findings.expected: the lateral posterior choroidal artery should be a sibling record (name), not a synonym of the medial artery
findings.basis: The record's own function text treats the medial and lateral posterior choroidal arteries as two distinct vessels with different origins ("the medial … arises from the P2 segment … while the lateral … arises more distally") and different targets (third ventricle/foramen region vs the body, atrium and temporal horn), and its afferent field says "the medial artery from the proximal P2 segment, the lateral from the distal P2". Listing the lateral artery as a synonym of the medial one makes the search index return the wrong vessel for a lateral-posterior-choroidal query, and the territory[] mix (vent-lateral-ventricle-body/atrium from the lateral artery + vent-third-ventricle from the medial) is a two-vessel union under a one-vessel name — which is also what creates VN-007's level gap.
findings.suggestedFix: keep the id, set name = "Posterior choroidal arteries (medial and lateral)", drop "lateral posterior choroidal artery" from synonyms and list it as the companion branch instead; or split into two records (vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery and vasc-posterior-lateral-choroidal-artery) when a mesh exists for the lateral one.
findings.notes: The record's contextNote already concedes the compromise ("Its lateral companion is not a separate element in the archive, so the record documents both branches and names this id after the one mesh that exists"), so a one-line naming fix is the smallest honest correction.

findings.claimed: tubeRadius = 0.42 au, calibreMm = 1.0; the record's own anchorNote says "1.0 mm calibre, the thinnest cranial nerve, at 1 au = 1.2 mm gives tubeRadius 0.42 au"
findings.expected: per the repository's own stated invariant r_au = d_mm / 2.4 at 1 au = 1.2 mm, calibreMm = 1.0 must give tubeRadius = 0.4167 ≈ 0.42 au — which is what the field holds — so the inconsistent field is calibreMm: the 0.42 au radius is d/2.4 of a 1.0 mm DIAMETER only if the radius is 0.5 mm, i.e. if calibreMm described a radius. Applied as the invariant demands (d = 1.0 mm as a diameter) the radius should be 0.83 au, twice the stored value.
findings.basis: The invariant and its expected table are asserted by the repo's own gate (scripts/verify/cranial-nerve-courses.mjs: "radius equals calibre ÷ 2.4 (1 au = 1.2 mm)" with the twelve expected radii printed as 0.71/1.67/1.25/0.42/1.88/0.79/0.79/1.17/0.83/1.00/0.63/0.75) and documented in docs/CONTENT_INVENTORY.md p.58 and docs/SWARM_V14_PLAN.md §3.4. Applying r = d/2.4 to the twelve declared calibres 1.7/4.0/3.0/1.0/4.5/1.9/1.9/2.8/2.0/2.4/1.5/1.8 mm yields 0.708/1.667/1.250/0.417/1.875/0.792/0.792/1.167/0.833/1.000/0.625/0.750 — matching the stored tubeRadius for ELEVEN of the twelve. The twelfth is CN IV: stored 0.42, formula 0.83, a factor-of-two discrepancy. The alternative reading (the stored 0.42 au is right and the declared 1.0 mm is a diameter that produced it) means the documented formula itself was applied as d/4.8 for this one nerve.
findings.suggestedFix: pick one and make the other field agree, then re-run verify:cranial-nerve-courses: (a) keep the rendered size and set calibreMm = 0.5 mm for CN IV so tubeRadius 0.42 = 0.5/1.2 (the radius in millimetres) — but then the field's meaning differs from the other eleven courses; or (b) keep calibreMm = 1.0 mm as the cisternal diameter and set tubeRadius = 0.83 au so the invariant holds — but that doubles the rendered nerve. Because r_au × 1.2 = 0.504 mm and d_rendered = 1.008 mm, option (b) is the internally consistent one and is also the one the four other sub-1.0 mm-diameter structures in the atlas would use; option (a) preserves the current look at the cost of a second meaning for calibreMm.
findings.notes: External cross-check on which rendered size is anatomical: high-resolution 3D MR of the cisternal trochlear nerve measures a mean diameter of 0.54 mm (range 0.35-0.96 mm) and reports a cadaver mean of 0.85 mm — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7963936/ — so the CURRENT rendered 1.01 mm diameter is already slightly generous and option (b) would make the thinnest cranial nerve the same thickness as the abducens. That is an argument for keeping the number and fixing the label, not for keeping the contradiction: the integrator should decide, and either choice is a one-field edit. Flagged major because CN IV is the unique offender, the dispatch explicitly asked whether the radius set is a plausible conversion of real calibres, and the answer is that eleven of twelve are and this one is not.

findings.claimed: the CN IV exit landmark surf-cn4-exit is registered at levels [lvl-pons-rostral (+2), lvl-midbrain-ic (+8)]
findings.expected: levels = [lvl-midbrain-ic] only
findings.basis: surf-cn4-exit.origin3d = [1.5, 7.5, -8]; the inferior colliculus (nuc-inferior-colliculus, origin3d.y = 8, and the level anchor text itself: "Midbrain — inferior colliculus (CN IV exit)") is at y = 8 = lvl-midbrain-ic. lvl-pons-rostral is y = +2, which is 6 au caudate to the landmark and is the pontomesencephalic junction, not the dorsal midbrain. The nerve record's own course text says the fibres "emerge on the DORSAL surface of the midbrain below the inferior colliculus", and no midbrain structure carries lvl-pons-rostral in the registry (nuc-trochlear is lvl-midbrain-ic only), so the extra level is an orphan: at lvl-pons-rostral the plate/level filter will show a CN IV rootlet marker on a pontine section where the nerve does not exist.
findings.suggestedFix: surf-cn4-exit.levels = ["lvl-midbrain-ic"].
findings.notes: The course record's own levels for CN IV ([lvl-pons-rostral, lvl-midbrain-ic]) are defensible because the course is a 4 cm cisternal chain that does descend to the pontomesencephalic junction; the landmark is a point, so only the landmark record is reported.

findings.claimed: foramen = "foramen ovale" (the course record's own field)
findings.expected: all three of the nerve's skull-base openings — superior orbital fissure (V1), foramen rotundum (V2) and foramen ovale (V3) — since the record's own course sentence already names all three
findings.basis: CN V is the only cranial nerve with three separate skull-base exits and the record's own course text says so ("V1 (ophthalmic) leaves through the superior orbital fissure, V2 (maxillary) through the foramen rotundum, and V3 (mandibular) through the foramen ovale"), while the machine-readable foramen field carries only the foramen ovale. The consequence is visible in the UI contract: the foramen is displayed as the nerve's single traverse, so a user asking "which foramen does the trigeminal use?" is given one third of the answer, and any downstream filter keyed on foramen will file CN V with the mandibular division. The 12-per-nerve gate (scripts/verify/cranial-nerve-courses.mjs §5) only requires that foramen be non-empty and a substring of the record's course sentence, so this passes the gate.
findings.suggestedFix: if the field is schema-fixed as a string, set foramen = "trigeminal ganglion → V1 superior orbital fissure, V2 foramen rotundum, V3 foramen ovale" (which is still a substring of the course sentence if the sentence is adjusted to match), or add a foramenExtra array for the multi-foramen nerve. Do not leave the single "foramen ovale" as the answer to a three-foramen question.
findings.notes: The same nerve is correctly described elsewhere (nrv-cn5-trigeminal.clinical: "Loss in V1 alone points to the superior orbital fissure … V2 alone to the foramen rotundum or the sinus; V3 alone to the foramen ovale"), so the defect is confined to the single-valued foramen field.

findings.claimed: waypoint 3 of 5 = [12, 19, 36] (the optic-canal entry on the intra-orbital→intracranial path), with waypoint 4 = [11, 19, 33] copied from tract-optic-nerve.waypoints[0] and waypoint 5 = [2, 23.5, 23.5] from tract-optic-nerve.waypoints[4]
findings.expected: the chain's own interior points should lie within the committed optic-nerve elements they are said to follow: x within the mesh x range (mirrored pair x ±[0.4, 27.0]) and z within the mesh z range [16.7, 63.2]
findings.basis: The two committed meshes left/right tract-optic-nerve-{l,r}.glb span x [0.4, 27.0] / [-26.9, -0.4], y [-5.1, 16.2], z [16.7, 63.2] au (read from the GLB POSITION accessors). All five CN II waypoints sit at x 2–26 and z 23.5–57 (inside), and y 16–23.5 — but the meshes' y tops out at 16.2, so the chain leaves the committed geometry after its first point and floats up to 7 au (8.4 mm) above the most superior vertex of the real optic-nerve mesh at its anterior end, while the in-file anchorNote claims the chain "follows the committed optic-nerve mesh" and quantifies the agreement as "within 9 per cent" on z only. The same mismatch exists between the two source records: tract-optic-nerve.waypoints[0] = [11, 19, 33] and the baked mesh's own extremes show the tract's superior limit is y = 16.2, i.e. the authored tract record and the baked mesh disagree by ~2.8 au in y at the same structure. The record's contextNote states "the subarachnoid (intracranial) segment … x ≈ 7, y ≈ 21, z ≈ 28".
findings.suggestedFix: report and reconcile the tract-optic-nerve record with its own baked meshes: either drop the authored y by ~4 au across the optic-pathway waypoints (tract-optic-nerve, ctx-optic-chiasm, nrv-cn2-optic course) so the chain lies inside the committed mesh, or re-state the anchorNote so it does not claim mesh agreement on an axis where the mesh disagrees. The CN II course's z agreement (51.2 au of arc vs 55.8 mm of mesh z) is real and should be kept.
findings.notes: Not a re-bake request: the meshes are frozen by verify:anatomy 27/27 and nothing here requires a different mesh — the authored numbers are what move. Reported at major rather than critical because the visual error is 8 mm along the optic nerve's own axis and the chain's two anchoring waypoints are exact copies of the committed tract waypoints, so the discrepancy is inherited rather than introduced.

findings.claimed: origin3d = [4.5, -18, 5], size3d = [1.6, 9, 2] (the schematic ellipsoid standing for the ascending cisternal course)
findings.expected: the schematic should stand where the nerve actually runs — lateral to the basilar artery in the prepontine cistern, i.e. z ≈ +8 to +12 at x ≈ 4.5 — with a note that no skull-base mesh exists to trace it to Dorello's canal
findings.basis: The ellipsoid spans z ∈ [3, 7] at x ∈ [2.9, 6.1]. The committed basilar artery mesh occupies x ∈ [-0.8, 1.4], z ∈ [11.3, 16.8], and the committed pons envelope ctx-pons-surface reaches z = 16.7 at its ventral surface — so a body at z 3–7 sits INSIDE the pons, not in the cistern beside the artery: the record's own bloodSupply says "it is the first nerve to be compressed by a vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia" and its course text says the nerve runs "through the prepontine cistern, hugging the clivus", neither of which can be true at z 3–7. The record's own first waypoint in the course table is [2.5, -24, 7.5] (the committed landmark, z = 7.5), so even the course's root position is more anterior than the ellipsoid's centre. The ellipsoid is a SCHEMATIC placement (the contextNote says so), so this is a schematic-position defect rather than a claim of anatomy.
findings.suggestedFix: origin3d = [4.5, -18, 11] with size3d [1.6, 9, 2], keeping it anterior to the pons ventral surface and lateral to the basilar; this also keeps it off the CN VII/VIII ellipsoids (z ≈ -6 to -10).
findings.notes: The ellipsoid does overlap its own exit landmark surf-cn6-exit [2.5, -24, 7.5] at its lower end as its contextNote claims, so only the anterior-posterior position is reported. The CN VI course record's own waypoints already go to z = 11–13, i.e. the course and the schematic disagree with each other.

findings.field: origin3d vs its own exit landmark surf-cn5-exit
findings.claimed: origin3d = [5.5, -9, -1], size3d = [2.6, 2, 4.5]; the contextNote says the ellipsoid "run[s] from the lateral pontine surface — where the rootlets leave at the landmark surf-cn5-exit ([7, -8, 6] … which the ellipsoid overlaps at its anterior end) — postero- and medially toward the petrous apex and Meckel's cave"
findings.expected: the schematic body and the exit landmark it names should touch (the landmark is on the brainstem surface and the ellipsoid is the nerve leaving that surface)
findings.basis: The overlap the contextNote asserts does not exist on the surface of the ellipsoid: the landmark is inside the ellipsoid's BOUNDING BOX in x and y (x [2.9, 8.1] contains 7; y [-11, -7] contains -8) but outside the ellipsoid itself — the ellipsoid's z half-axis is 4.5 about z = -1 so it reaches only z = 3.5, and the landmark is at z = 6. Measured distance from the ellipsoid surface to its own landmark: CN V 2.90 au (3.5 mm), CN VII 2.09, CN IV 1.97, CN III 1.88, CN VI 1.81, CN IX 1.27, CN X 1.09, CN XII 0.26, CN XI 0.18, CN VIII 0.08 (a numeric surface sampling of all ten landmarked nerve ellipsoids). CN V is the worst of the ten, and it is the only record whose prose asserts the contact; the others are silent and simply sit close. The consequence is a visible 3.5 mm gap between the trigeminal body and its own root-exit marker in the 3D view at lvl-pons-middle.
findings.suggestedFix: move the schematic onto the surface it stands for: origin3d ≈ [6, -8.5, 4] with size3d [2.6, 2, 4.5] — this contains surf-cn5-exit (normalised value 0.41) and nuc-trigeminal-motor (0.65) — or rewrite the contextNote so it does not claim an overlap that the numbers deny.
findings.notes: Kept at suspect/minor rather than wrong: the ellipsoid is explicitly documented as a SCHEMATIC placement, and the true cisternal course of CN V does run postero-medially at this depth, so the body is not in an absurd place — it is 3.5 mm off its own landmark, which is the largest such gap in the nerve set and the only one the record claims is zero.

findings.claimed: "The pupillomotor fibres run on the superficial dorsomedial surface of the cisternal nerve, where the posterior communicating artery crosses it"
findings.expected: "…on the superficial superomedial (dorsomedial) surface…" — or simply "on the superficial surface", since the load-bearing fact is that the parasympathetic fibres are superficial and the somatic fibres deep
findings.basis: The claim is directionally right (the pupillomotor/parasympathetic fibres are superficial and the somatic fibres deep, which is why compression involves the pupil and microvascular ischaemia spares it) but the compass direction is questionable: the standard description places them superomedially/dorsomedially on the nerve, and the posterior communicating artery crosses BELOW and medial to the nerve's inferior surface, so "dorsomedial … where the artery crosses it" is internally tensioned. External basis: StatPearls, Neuroanatomy, Cranial Nerve 3 — "Somatic (voluntary) nerve fibers are bundled deep inside the nerve, while the autonomic (involuntary) fibers surround the somatic fibers around the outside of the nerve" (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537126/).
findings.suggestedFix: replace "on the superficial dorsomedial surface" with "in the superficial (outer) part of the nerve, the pupillomotor fibres being the most superficial — which is why compression dilates the pupil early and microvascular ischaemia spares it", leaving the fibre-depth rule as the stated reason and dropping the contested compass direction.
findings.notes: The same note appears verbatim in the CN III course record and in the PComA record's clinical text, so one correction covers three places. Suspect rather than wrong because the atlas's phrasing is a defensible paraphrase of the depth-based rule and I cannot establish the direction from the repository.

findings.claimed: Superior salivatory nucleus (nuc-superior-salivatory) is listed under connections.afferent while the same record's efferent list also carries its fibres ("Greater petrosal nerve to the pterygopalatine ganglion … and chorda tympani …"), and nrv-cn5-trigeminal has the identical pattern (nuc-trigeminal-motor under afferent + its fibres under efferent)
findings.expected: one direction per connection: a nucleus whose axons FORM the nerve is not an afferent of the nerve
findings.basis: The afferent headings in these records are being used as "central structures this nerve links" rather than as anatomical afferents, and in seven of the twelve records the preamble says so explicitly ("the nerve itself carries no afferents" — CN III, IV, V, VI, XII). For CN VII and CN V the heading is load-bearing in the opposite direction: the efferent lists name the same nucleus's fibres, so the same neuron is counted as an input and an output of the same nerve. The dispatch rule is explicit that "an efferent listed as afferent is a defect". Because the same convention is applied consistently and is documented in the prose, this is a schema-semantics defect rather than a false claim.
findings.suggestedFix: for the five purely-motor or mixed nerves, rename or re-populate the afferent heading: put the motor/secretomotor nuclei under a "central connections" heading in both prose and data, and keep afferent only for structures that genuinely deliver fibres to the nerve (CN VII: geniculate ganglion/nervus intermedius taste and the concha sensory zone, already correctly present as prose).
findings.notes: The direction of the clinical content is not affected: every statement about which fibres fail in which lesion is correct.

findings.recordId: nuc-trigeminal-motor (linked by nrv-cn5-trigeminal and by the CN V course anchorId)
findings.claimed: laterality = "paired" with origin3d = [4, -8, 4] and size3d = [2, 2.5, 1.8]
findings.expected: laterality = "midline" with x = 0 (as the other nuclei of midline/bilateral structures are authored) — or keep "paired" and set x = 0, since the committed mesh is bilateral
findings.basis: The glb registered for this record, src/assets/anatomy/nuc-trigeminal-motor.glb, spans x [-5.8, 5.9] — a single bilateral mesh, produced by the recipe's bilateral union (scripts/anatomy-recipes/nuclei.mjs: `bilateral(field, paired)` mirrors only when laterality === 'paired'). The record declares laterality = 'paired', which makes the runtime draw the same canonical GLB at +x and -x (SceneLayers), so the structure renders as four half-nuclei rather than two. The same defect applies to nuc-principal-sensory-v (mesh x [-7.0, 7.0]), nuc-vestibular-medial (x ±5.3), nuc-cochlear-ventral (x ±7.8) and several other brainstem nuclei. Its sibling nuc-spinal-trigeminal is authored the other way (midline, origin3d = [0, ...]) with a comparable bilateral mesh.
findings.suggestedFix: choose one convention for bilateral brainstem nuclei and apply it to all of them: either laterality = "midline" with origin3d.x = 0 (matching nuc-spinal-trigeminal and the oculomotor/trochlear/hypoglossal pattern) or laterality = "paired" with origin3d.x = 0 so that the mirror is a no-op.
findings.notes: Reported here rather than to the nucleus auditor because CN V's efferent field names this record as its origin and the CN V course is anchored on its origin3d, so the count of trigeminal motor nuclei on screen is part of this nerve's rendering.

findings.field: modality / course (spot-verification of an explicitly named audit target)
findings.claimed: modality = "Motor only, with two roots of different origin: branchial motor (cranial root, to the larynx through the recurrent laryngeal nerve) and somatic motor (spinal root, to sternocleidomastoid and trapezius)"; course gives the foramen magnum for the spinal root and the jugular foramen for the common trunk
findings.expected: exactly this
findings.basis: External: StatPearls, Neuroanatomy, Cranial Nerve 11 — "CN XI also contributes indirectly to intrinsic laryngeal musculature function via its cranial component, which arises from the nucleus ambiguus and merges with the vagus nerve (CN X) to supply motor fibers to the larynx, pharynx, and soft palate" (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK507722/), and the two-foramen arrangement is the standard account. Internal: the record's own bloodSupply ties the spinal root to the V3 segment of the vertebral artery, and its afferent[] correctly puts the spinal root's origin in the C1–C5/6 anterior horn and names no registry record for it.
findings.notes: Verified because the dispatch named it as a required check. No correction needed; the two-root, two-foramen description is complete and the spinal root is correctly carried on the course chain (the displayed path stops in the neck rather than pretending to reach the abdomen).

findings.field: foramen (full sweep of the twelve skull-base openings)
findings.claimed: I cribriform plate; II optic canal; III superior orbital fissure; IV superior orbital fissure; V foramen ovale; VI superior orbital fissure; VII internal acoustic meatus; VIII internal acoustic meatus; IX jugular foramen; X jugular foramen; XI jugular foramen; XII hypoglossal canal
findings.expected: exactly this list
findings.basis: Terminologia Anatomica / standard foramina: I cribriform plate of the ethmoid; II optic canal; III and IV superior orbital fissure; V1 superior orbital fissure, V2 foramen rotundum, V3 foramen ovale; VI superior orbital fissure; VII and VIII internal acoustic meatus; IX, X and XI jugular foramen (XI's spinal root additionally through the foramen magnum, which the record states); XII hypoglossal canal. Internal consistency: every foramen string is a substring of its own record's course sentence (the repo's own gate asserts this), CN IX correctly reads "pars nervosa" and CN X/XI "pars vascularis" of the jugular foramen, and the only multi-foramen nerve (V) is reported separately as VN-018.
findings.notes: No cranial nerve is routed through a wrong skull-base opening. The "VI and the ophthalmic veins through the superior orbital fissure/cavernous sinus" check also passes: CN VI is routed through Dorello's canal → cavernous sinus → superior orbital fissure, which is correct, and (V1) is correctly given the superior orbital fissure.

findings.basis: Measured independently against the records (not against the gate): CN III waypoint 1 = [0, 14, -4] = nuc-oculomotor.origin3d exactly, and waypoint 3 = [2, 9.5, 8.5] = surf-cn3-exit exactly (deviation 0.000 au); CN IV [0, 8, -5] = nuc-trochlear and [1.5, 7.5, -8] = surf-cn4-exit (0.000); CN V [4, -8, 4] = nuc-trigeminal-motor and [7, -8, 6] = surf-cn5-exit (0.000); CN VI [1.5, -18, -4] = nuc-abducens and [2.5, -24, 7.5] = surf-cn6-exit (0.000, waypoint 3 — note waypoint 4 [4, -20, 13] is 0.5 au from the landmark so the literal-landmark tolerance is met by waypoint 3, not by the nearest point); CN VII [4, -19, -2] = nuc-facial and [6.5, -23, -3] = surf-cn7-exit (0.000); CN VIII [6.8, -22, -4.5] = surf-cn8-exit (0.000) with its root [3.5, -14, -5.5] = nuc-vestibular-medial; CN IX [3.5, -31, -4] = nuc-ambiguus and [5, -31, 4.5] = surf-cn9-exit (0.000); CN X [2, -32, -7] = nuc-dmv and [5, -34, 4.5] = surf-cn10-exit (0.000); CN XI [3.5, -31, -4] = nuc-ambiguus and [6, -43, 2] = surf-cn11-exit (0.000); CN XII [0, -31, -4] = nuc-hypoglossal and [3.5, -32, 6.5] = surf-cn12-exit (0.000); CN I's chain ENDS on its own origin3d [8, 12, 48] (its anchorId is legitimately empty — the nerve has no brainstem root and no exit landmark, which the record documents); CN II's waypoints 4 and 5 are literal copies of tract-optic-nerve.waypoints[0] and [4].
